rationale: All 6 candidates are direct matches on concept and endpoint (trait_reported/trait_efo are abdominal aortic aneurysm; phenotyping_reported is AAA, with PGS000753 explicitly prevalent AAA). The strongest PRS-comparable evidence in the pool is for PGS000753: it reports an effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), which is more directly interpretable for PRS discrimination than full-model AUROC/C-index values. Competing models mainly report full-model discrimination (e.g., AUROC 0.868 for PGS001784; C-index 0.882 for PGS003973) without clear PRS-only AUROC, and domain guidance cautions these can be largely covariate-driven; PGS001784 does provide a covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.014661, but it comes from a portability/framework-style paper and the metric advantage over others is modest. Several other candidates have missing PRS-only metrics and/or unknown covariates, limiting confident ranking. Therefore a direct match exists, but the evidence is insufficiently decisive for a high-confidence single best choice.

All four candidates are direct matches in the sense that their mapped EFO terms align with alcohol dependence/alcohol dependence measurement, and their phenotyping is alcohol use disorder (AUD). Among them, PGS002738 is the most directly aligned to the target trait at the concept level (trait_efo="alcohol dependence"; trait_reported/phenotyping_reported="Alcohol use disorder") and provides the strongest visible discriminative evidence via an odds ratio for top 10% vs rest (OR=1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51) in European evaluation. The main limitation is that none of the candidates report PRS-only AUC/R2; PGS002738 also has unknown covariates and multiple performance records without detailed breakdown here, reducing comparability and preventing a high-confidence selection. PGS000201/PGS000202 have explicit incremental ΔR² values (0.01192 and 0.00456) with disclosed covariates, but they are framed as "Problematic alcohol use" with a DSM-5 criteria count endpoint and show weaker incremental signal than the OR evidence in PGS002738, leaving the overall choice somewhat uncertain.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target concept (trait_efo = alcoholic liver cirrhosis) with broadly aligned endpoints in phenotyping_reported. However, none reports clearly PRS-only discrimination (PGS-only AUROC/R²), so cross-model ranking must rely on endpoint fidelity plus the limited available performance/effect-size evidence.

PGS001777 is preferred because it is disease-focused on alcohol-related cirrhosis and provides the most directly PRS-informative signal among the set via a large risk gradient (Odds Ratio top 20% vs bottom 20% = 6.18, with AUROC 0.671 reported) despite using only 3 variants. PGS000704 reports a higher full-model C-index (0.711) but this is explicitly a full-model metric with demographic covariates and lacks PRS-only metrics; its per-SD HR=1.18 suggests only modest standalone PRS signal. PGS004913 reports an R²=0.029 and OR top vs bottom deciles=4.4, but the R² is not explicitly PRS-only and the evidence package is limited (no classification metrics shown).

Main limitation: the available metrics are not clearly comparable PRS-only measures across candidates (full-model AUROC/C-index and unspecified R²), and covariates are unknown for PGS001777, so the selection is supported but not definitive.

All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris (trait_efo=angina pectoris) with generally aligned phenotyping strings (e.g., ICD10 I20, PheCode 411.3, or doctor-diagnosed angina). Among models with explicit PRS-comparable metrics, the snpnet UKB framework scores (PGS001260/PGS001261/PGS001262) report PGS-only AUROC (~0.58) and PGS R2 (~0.012–0.013), which are interpretable and below the provided heritability ceiling (h2_obs ~0.009–0.014; h2_liability ~0.134), supporting metric plausibility. PGS001262 is preferred within this sibling set because it has the strongest incremental evidence in the selected European validation record (highest PGS-only AUROC 0.58683 and PGS R2 0.01304, and the largest incremental AUROC 0.0098) with basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs) and a direct doctor-diagnosed angina endpoint. However, confidence is not high because several newer ICD10/PheCode-based models (e.g., PGS004457/PGS004527; PGS005048/PGS005052/PGS005057/PGS005058) report only full-model C-index or per-SD OR without clear PGS-only discrimination, making cross-model performance comparability limited; additionally, the chosen model comes from a pan-trait UKB sparse-PRS framework publication, which domain guidance flags as often less externally robust than disease-focused development, but the context does not provide a clearly superior disease-focused alternative with comparable PRS-only metrics.

All 9 candidates are direct matches to ankylosing spondylitis by trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (mostly direct case/control; one time-to-event). Among the pool, PGS001267 provides the clearest PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports both PGS-only AUROC (0.7265) and PGS-only R2 (0.0988) plus full-model AUROC with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), and its PRS-only R2 is below the provided heritability ceiling (h2_liability=0.3993), passing the sanity check. Competing UKB portability models (PGS001876, PGS002089) lack AUROC/R2 and only report partial-r, and the Taiwan EAS models report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates (not PRS-only comparable), limiting their interpretability for PRS ranking. Remaining limitation: PGS001268 is a near-twin with slightly higher full-model AUROC but uses a time-to-event endpoint, and the evidence does not clearly establish whether the generic case/control (PGS001267) or TTE (PGS001268) is preferable for the target’s generic disease-risk framing; additionally, the selected best model comes from a pan-trait UKB framework paper, which domain guidance flags as a generalizability concern, lowering confidence from high.

Among the 8 returned candidates, only four are direct matches to the target disease concept (aortic stenosis): PGS005252 and PGS005254 (trait_reported/trait_efo = aortic stenosis) plus PGS005255/PGS005256 (aortic valve function measures but phenotyping_reported still states incident aortic stenosis). The remaining four models are for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and are not direct matches.

PGS005252 is best supported within the direct-match set because it has clear endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: incident aortic stenosis cases; trait_efo: aortic stenosis), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDPred2) with a large variant set (1,119,377), and provides both a time-to-event effect size (HR=1.92) and a reported discrimination metric (C-index=0.87) in European evaluation. Competing direct-match candidates (PGS005254/PGS005255/PGS005256) report HRs (1.64 and 1.53) but provide no discrimination metrics in the visible metadata, making them less well-supported on comparable performance evidence.

Main limitation: the reported C-index for PGS005252 is a full-model metric with many clinical covariates (e.g., diabetes, hypertension, CAD, hyperlipidemia, BMI, smoking, renal failure), so it cannot be interpreted as PRS-only performance; no PRS-only AUROC/R² is provided for any aortic stenosis candidate here, which lowers certainty and keeps confidence at Moderate.

Direct-match candidates for the exact target trait (arthritis; trait_efo="arthritis") are present, notably PGS001135 ("Arthritis (nos)") and the Commun Biol "M13 (Other arthritis)" models (PGS004477, PGS004547). PGS001135 has the strongest endpoint fidelity for generic arthritis risk (phenotyping_reported="Arthritis (nos)") and provides PRS-comparable metrics (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.53928; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.00291) plus a European-selected validation record (full-model AUROC=0.67424, incremental AUROC=0.00314). Its PRS-only R2 is below the provided heritability ceiling (h2_liability=0.0610), passing the sanity check. The main limitation is that PGS001135 comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework study ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as tending to generalize poorly versus disease-focused studies; however, among the exact arthritis EFO matches shown, the alternatives (PGS004477/PGS004547) lack comparable discrimination metrics (only ORs reported) and have less explicit endpoint detail beyond "M13 (Other arthritis)", leaving PGS001135 as the best-supported direct-match on visible evidence.

All listed candidates are direct matches to asthma (trait_efo=asthma), but they vary in endpoint fidelity and in whether reported metrics are PRS-comparable vs covariate-inflated. PGS001344 (snpnet; asthma diagnosed by doctor) has strong endpoint fidelity for generic asthma risk (explicit doctor diagnosis), reports both PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates=0.64568; PGS R2 no covariates=0.05973) and full-model metrics (AUROC=0.66621; R2=0.07596) with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), making its performance evidence more comparable than models that only report full-model AUROC or have unknown/heavier covariates. Competing direct-match models include PGS002727 (pediatric asthma; OR=1.57; AUROC=0.66 but covariates unknown and endpoint is pediatric-specific), PGS002248 (childhood asthma by age 8; very high full-model AUROC=0.85 but appears to be a packaged clinical model ‘CAPP model’ and is childhood-specific), and several framework/portability-style scores (e.g., PGS001341/001343/001346; PGS001849/PGS002061) with less disease-focused context or less directly PRS-comparable reporting. Remaining limitation: the pool contains multiple plausible asthma PRS with heterogeneous endpoints (incident, pediatric, algorithmic, ICD code) and many lack clean PRS-only metrics, so while PGS001344 is best-supported from the visible evidence, the overall evidence base is mixed, keeping confidence below high.

All 6 candidates are direct matches at the EFO level (atopic eczema), but several have endpoint mismatches: PGS003459/PGS003486/PGS004903 are evaluated on paradoxical (biologic-treatment–associated) eczema in psoriasis patients rather than generic atopic eczema risk. PGS001773 targets moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis and reports very high full-model AUROC/R² (0.93/0.49) with demographic/ethnicity covariates, but lacks PRS-only metrics and the R² appears implausibly high relative to the provided atopic eczema heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0709; h2_liability=0.1288), suggesting the reported discrimination is likely covariate-driven or otherwise non-comparable. Between the remaining incident atopic dermatitis models, PGS002755 and PGS004587 both use an incident endpoint and report similar HR (1.249 vs 1.153) with similar covariates; PGS002755 is preferred due to stronger effect size evidence (higher HR with CI) and a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with broad variant coverage (1,090,702 variants). Limitation: none of the candidates provide clearly PRS-only AUROC/R², so the selection relies on endpoint fidelity and effect-size/method signals rather than directly comparable PRS discrimination metrics.

Direct-match candidates for atrial fibrillation are abundant (61 models) with generally consistent concept alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported largely AF or incident AF). Among them, PGS005168 is best supported by the visible evidence because it is a disease-focused, large multi-cohort AF meta-analysis PRS (Nat Genet; many contributing cohorts listed) with a direct AF endpoint and strong reported discrimination in the selected European validation record (C-index 0.8718 with CI 0.8657–0.878) plus a per-SD HR ~1.67. However, the evidence remains insufficient for a clearly high-confidence ‘best’ choice because many competing direct AF models also report strong full-model metrics (including several with C-index ~0.82–0.83 in MVP-derived evaluations and others with AUROC ~0.75–0.78), and most reported metrics are full-model (covariate-influenced) rather than explicitly PRS-only; additionally, PGS005168’s covariates include CHARGE-AF (a named clinical risk calculator), which domain guidance flags as risk-wrapper packaging that reduces comparability of the reported discrimination to standalone PRS performance.

All four candidates are direct matches in the sense that their trait_efo includes atrial flutter, but only PGS001263 has phenotype alignment that is specific to the target (phenotyping_reported and trait_reported both “Atrial flutter”), whereas PGS001339/PGS001841/PGS002050 use the broader combined endpoint “Atrial fibrillation and flutter” (including a time-to-event variant for PGS001339). PGS001263 also provides explicit PRS-comparable metrics (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.61716; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.02517) and these are below the provided heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0157; h2_liability=0.1443), so they are not obviously inconsistent. However, the strongest-looking AUROC shown for PGS001263 (0.78179) is a full-model metric with covariates and should not be treated as PRS-only evidence; and the alternative models from the portability paper (PGS001841/PGS002050) lack AUC/R2 and only report partial-r, making cross-model performance comparison incomplete. Given the framework-study origin of PGS001263 and limited comparable performance evidence across all candidates, the selection is direct but not high-certainty.

Both candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo, but PGS000327 has substantially better endpoint fidelity: phenotyping_reported is explicitly “Autism spectrum disorder” (a direct clinical disease endpoint), whereas PGS002790’s phenotyping_reported is “Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)”, creating an endpoint mismatch despite the surface ASD label. PGS000327 also provides supportive PRS-quality evidence (OR per SD 1.33 with CI 1.30–1.36 and an R² metric reported as 0.0245) with only basic covariates (genetic PCs, genotyping wave) and a disease-focused publication context (Nat Genet ASD GWAS). However, confidence is limited because neither model reports clearly PRS-only discrimination metrics (e.g., PGS-only AUROC or covariates-regressed-out R²), and the reported R² fields may reflect full-model/partial metrics rather than strictly PRS-comparable performance.

All 20 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo (basal cell carcinoma), but they differ in endpoint fidelity and strength of reported validation evidence. PGS000452 has clean endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: Basal cell carcinoma) with only basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4) and shows the strongest visible performance/effect evidence among the comparable MGI-evaluated siblings: full-model AUROC 0.632 (0.616–0.647), strong per-SD OR 1.663 (1.57–1.761), and the largest reported Nagelkerke pseudo-R² (0.0487) in this set. Competing close models (e.g., PGS000454/PGS000456/PGS000458) have very similar AUROC/OR but slightly weaker or comparable metrics, while PGS000119 has a slightly higher AUROC (0.64) but lacks the additional supporting pseudo-R²/other-metrics detail and comes from a different publication family. Newer 2023 models (PGS003416/PGS003417) have less endpoint-specific phenotyping_reported (“Keratinocyte cancers”) and provide only effect sizes without AUROC/R², and PGS005207 is explicitly restricted to childhood cancer survivors (endpoint mismatch for generic BCC risk). Main limitation: across the pool, metrics are largely full-model (not PRS-only), so cross-model comparability is imperfect; the choice is therefore based on the best-supported, endpoint-faithful candidate with the strongest available validation package in the provided metadata.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target trait via trait_efo/phenotyping_reported. PGS000924 targets a broader composite endpoint (porphyrin + bilirubin metabolism) and is explicitly time-to-event from a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse-score framework paper; despite high reported AUROC, this context and endpoint breadth/time-to-event framing are warning signals for generalizability and make the metric less decisive. PGS001824 and PGS002032 both exactly match the disease concept (Disorders of bilirubin excretion; trait_efo=bilirubin metabolism disease) and come from the same portability study with identical reported partial-r (0.0716) and similar covariates, so performance evidence does not separate them. Between these two near-clones, PGS002032 is structurally preferred because it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with far more variants (19,768 vs 22), which is a positive signal when endpoints and metrics are otherwise indistinguishable. Confidence is only Moderate because neither portability model reports PRS-only AUROC/R² (only partial-r), and the remaining differentiation relies mainly on method/variant-count heuristics rather than directly comparable discrimination metrics.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target umbrella trait (bipolar disorder spectrum) via trait_reported/trait_efo, but endpoint fidelity is unclear/possibly misaligned because phenotyping_reported fields are non-diagnostic (cognitive/behavioral measures) rather than bipolar disorder case-control/diagnosis endpoints. Performance evidence is limited and not clearly PRS-comparable: only small full_model_r2/partial R² values are shown (no PGS-only AUROC/R², no effect sizes), and covariates are basic (age, PCs1-3) across all models, offering little differentiation. Given indistinguishable study family/method (all SDPR, EUR-only GWAS/EVAL) and similar validation sizes, PGS002786 is selected only because it is the broadest concept match (bipolar disorder rather than subtype I/II), but this is a marginal advantage and does not resolve the endpoint-fidelity concern.

All three candidates are direct matches at the broad level of “blood coagulation disease,” but none is a clearly high-quality choice from the visible evidence. PGS001033 maps directly to the target EFO (“blood coagulation disease”) and provides the most interpretable discrimination evidence (includes PGS-only AUROC 0.634 and PGS-only R² 0.0578; full-model AUROC 0.656 with only basic covariates), whereas PGS001826 and PGS002034 target a narrower congenital clotting-factor deficiency EFO and report only partial correlation (~0.056) without AUROC/R², limiting comparability. However, PGS001033 is from a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse-score framework (“across 813 traits”) and is extremely sparse (1 variant) with a time-to-event phenotype, both warning signals for generalizability and endpoint fidelity. Given these competing limitations (framework+sparsity for PGS001033 vs narrower phenotype and weaker metrics for PGS001826/PGS002034), the selection is uncertain and therefore sub-optimal.

Direct-match candidates for breast carcinoma are abundant in the provided context. Among them, PGS004153 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) is the strongest-supported choice based on the visible evidence: it has exact concept alignment (trait_efo=breast carcinoma; phenotyping_reported=Breast cancer), uses an explicitly multi-score aggregation approach (a positive structural signal per the provided domain_knowledge), and shows the best reported discrimination within the clearly comparable cluster from the same publication family (full-model AUROC 0.6625 with accompanying OR 1.83 and R² 0.0764; covariates listed as 0, suggesting no covariate-driven inflation). The main limitation is that performance reporting is still largely full-model (no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R² field here), and several other direct-match models are close in AUROC within the same 2023 benchmarking family (e.g., PGS004040/PGS004025), so while PGS004153 is preferred, the margin is not decisive enough for High confidence.

All 10 candidates are direct matches to celiac disease via trait_efo, but they vary in endpoint fidelity and availability of PRS-comparable performance. PGS001301 has a direct/near-direct endpoint (“Malabsorption/coeliac disease”) and is the only candidate here reporting explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.82867; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.14224) alongside full-model AUROC=0.83351 with basic covariates, making its performance evidence more comparable than models that report only full-model AUROC (e.g., PGS000040 AUROC=0.9 with unknown covariates) or only partial correlation (e.g., PGS002067). However, PGS001301 comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as often less externally robust than disease-focused scores; additionally, its phenotype is a composite label rather than a pure celiac diagnosis. These limitations prevent a high-confidence ‘best’ despite being the best-supported option from the visible, PRS-comparable metrics.

All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=cervical carcinoma; phenotyping_reported is cervical cancer/incident cervical cancer). Among them, PGS001299 provides the most PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports PGS-only AUROC (0.55215) and PGS R² (no covariates) (0.00263), plus incremental AUROC (0.00676), whereas the other candidates mainly report full-model AUROC/C-index and/or HR that are less directly comparable to standalone PRS performance. However, confidence is limited because PGS001299 comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework study (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as often less externally robust than disease-focused scores; and several disease-focused cervical-cancer models (e.g., PGS003428 LDpred genome-wide; PGS000073/PGS000784 GWAS-hits) lack PRS-only metrics in the provided context, preventing a clean, high-confidence head-to-head comparison.

All 6 candidates are direct matches to cholelithiasis at the concept level (either exact cholelithiasis/K80 or a closely related composite endpoint including cholelithiasis). PGS001174 is preferred because it is the only model in the set with clearly reported PRS-comparable performance metrics, including PGS-only AUROC (0.62342) and PGS-only R2 (0.02808) plus incremental AUROC (0.04311) under basic covariates, and these PRS-only metrics are plausibly below the provided heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0214; h2_liability=0.1372), supporting interpretability. Main limitation: PGS001174 is from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper and uses a time-to-event phenotype, both of which are warning signals for external generalization; meanwhile several newer exact-endpoint K80/cholelithiasis models (PGS004476/PGS004546/PGS005150) are disease-labeled but lack comparable AUC/R2 evidence (only modest OR/beta reported and covariates unknown for two), preventing a high-confidence, clearly best-supported choice.

Multiple direct-match CKD candidates are present (22 total). PGS002237 is best supported by endpoint fidelity and disease-focused study context: it targets CKD stage 3+ with an explicit clinical eGFR threshold (eGFR <45 ml/min/1.73m2) and comes from a CKD-focused publication (“Genome-wide polygenic score to predict chronic kidney disease across ancestries.”, Nat Med) with multi-ancestry evaluation. It also reports a reasonably strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.47) and an AUROC (0.78) in the selected European validation record. Main limitation: the reported AUROC is a full-model metric with substantial clinical covariates (e.g., hypertension, diabetes, BMI, medication use), and no PGS-only AUROC/R² is provided, so the PRS-specific contribution cannot be cleanly compared across candidates; this keeps confidence at Moderate despite strong endpoint alignment.

Direct-match candidates for COPD are present (multiple models with trait_efo = chronic obstructive pulmonary disease). Among them, PGS001783 is preferred because it is phenotype-aligned (phenotyping_reported: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) and comes from a multi-biobank, multi-ancestry GWAS framework using a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto) with a PRS-comparable metric reported (Nagelkerke R2 covariates-regressed-out = 0.038092), which is consistent with the provided COPD heritability ceiling (h2_liability=0.0388) and suggests a strong PRS signal relative to other candidates that either report much smaller PGS-only R2 (e.g., snpnet models ~0.002–0.003) or only partial correlation/effect size without comparable PRS-only metrics. Limitation: evidence remains incomplete/heterogeneous across candidates (several report only full-model AUROC or only OR without PRS-only AUROC/R2; covariates are unknown for some newer models), and PGS001783’s AUROC is not explicitly PRS-only (full_model AUROC=0.74), so the selection is supported but not definitive.

All 6 candidates are direct matches at the disease level, but several are subtype-restricted to alcohol-related/alcoholic cirrhosis (PGS000704, PGS001777, PGS004913) or have phenotype ambiguity (PGS000776 is labeled cirrhosis but phenotyping_reported references an at-risk NAFLD time-to-event hospitalization endpoint). Among the models explicitly aligned to generic cirrhosis (trait_efo = cirrhosis of liver), PGS004621 has the strongest overall evidence package in this context: endpoint fidelity is directly ‘Cirrhosis’, it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant coverage (1,089,806), and it reports a representative discrimination metric (AUROC 0.68) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs) and EUR evaluation. However, confidence is limited because the reported AUROC appears to be a full-model metric (not explicitly PRS-only), and competing generic-cirrhosis candidates (e.g., PGS000726) provide effect-size evidence but lack comparable AUROC/R2, making cross-model performance comparison incomplete.

ontology: congenital vitamin k-dependent coagulation factors deficiency
rationale: Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS001826, PGS002034), and both align on the same endpoint fields: trait_efo matches the target trait and phenotyping_reported/trait_reported are identical (“Congenital deficiency of other clotting factors (including factor VII)”). Both come from the same UKB portability publication, use similar basic covariates, have the same training cohort context and validation sample size, and report essentially identical European validation partial correlation (0.0562 vs 0.0563 with overlapping CIs), so performance evidence does not clearly separate them. Given the domain guidance to use structural signals when PRS-only AUC/R2 are absent and candidates are otherwise near-clones, PGS002034 is mildly preferred because it uses LDpred2 (genome-wide shrinkage) with far more variants (32,552 vs 45), which is generally a stronger single-score construction for polygenic signal capture. The main limitation is that both models are from a portability/framework-style UKB study and only provide a modest partial-r metric (no PRS-only AUC/R2 or effect sizes), making the direct-match recommendation less strongly supported overall.

Both candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all state corneal dystrophy) and come from the same UKB portability publication with similar basic covariates and the same reported validation context. The main differentiator in the visible evidence is PRS-comparable performance: PGS002042 shows a higher selected European partial correlation (partial-r 0.0471, CI 0.033–0.0611) than PGS001835 (0.0384, CI 0.0243–0.0525), and it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with far more variants (59,944 vs 38), which is a supportive structural signal when endpoints are otherwise identical. Confidence is only Moderate because both models are from a portability/framework-style study (not clearly disease-focused) and neither reports standard PRS-only AUROC/R2 or effect sizes, limiting the strength of empirical differentiation beyond partial-r.

Direct-match candidates for coronary artery disease are abundant (85). Among them, PGS003725 is a direct CAD endpoint (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all coronary artery disease) and comes from a disease-focused multi-ancestry PRS study (Nat Med: “A multi-ancestry polygenic risk score improves risk prediction for coronary artery disease”), with strong per-SD effect sizes reported (HR=1.75; OR=2.14) and broad multi-ancestry evaluation listed (AFR/AMR/EAS/EUR/MAE/SAS). This combination of endpoint fidelity plus strong effect-size evidence and multi-ancestry context provides the best-supported direct-match package in the visible metadata. Main limitation: many candidates report only full-model AUROC (often covariate-influenced) and PGS003725 lacks explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2 in the provided record, so confidence is reduced and some alternatives (e.g., PGS000018 with high full-model AUROC=0.89 but prevalent endpoint and small validation n=3,309; PGS000013 with full-model AUROC=0.81 and PRS-only R2=0.04) remain plausible but are not clearly superior given the stronger effect-size evidence and multi-ancestry framing for PGS003725.

All three candidates are direct matches to Crohn disease by trait_efo, and PGS001331/PGS001330 also have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (Crohn’s disease; one is time-to-event). Among the two near-clone snpnet models from the same pan-trait UKB framework paper, PGS001331 has slightly stronger PRS-comparable metrics in European validation (PGS-only AUROC 0.579 vs 0.576; PGS-only R2 0.00677 vs 0.00621; incremental AUROC 0.027 vs 0.024) with essentially identical basic covariates, making it the best-supported choice within that sibling pair. PGS004254 reports a much higher AUROC (0.72) and OR (2.18), but the AUROC appears to be full-model only (no PGS-only AUROC/R2 provided), so it is not directly comparable as PRS evidence per the provided domain guidance; this prevents a high-confidence promotion based on that single metric. Overall, a direct-match exists, but comparability limitations (full-model-only metrics for PGS004254; framework-origin penalty for the snpnet scores) keep the decision sub-optimal rather than high-quality.

Direct-match dementia models are present (e.g., PGS000929/PGS000946/PGS001827/PGS002035/PGS004281–PGS004284/PGS004318/PGS005170). Among these, PGS005170 has the strongest endpoint fidelity for the target (phenotyping_reported: incident all-cause dementia; trait_efo: dementia) and a structurally favorable approach (integrative PRS combining 24 component PRSs), which domain knowledge flags as a consistent positive signal versus single-score constructions. However, the evidence remains limited for a clearly high-quality pick because the reported AUROC (0.761) appears to be a full-model metric (no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2 shown), and the validation sample size is small (n=2,032) relative to several other dementia candidates; additionally, other direct-match candidates report explicit PRS-only metrics (e.g., PGS000929/PGS000946) but come from pan-trait UKB framework scores that domain knowledge warns may generalize poorly. This leaves PGS005170 as the best-supported direct-match overall, but with unresolved comparability/robustness limitations.

Direct-match candidates are present for depressive disorder / major depressive disorder. Among the models with clear endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported = "Depression" or "Major Depressive Disorder"), PGS002036 is preferred because it targets depressive disorder directly (trait_efo="depressive disorder", phenotyping_reported="Depression"), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) appropriate for a highly polygenic trait, and has an explicit PRS-comparable metric (partial correlation 0.0556, EUR validation record). Key limitation: the evidence is still insufficient for a high-quality designation because most candidates lack PRS-only AUROC/R², several alternatives are similarly well-aligned (e.g., PGS003333/PGS003576 family) but report only full-model or non-PRS-comparable metrics, and some reported metrics in the pool are clearly non-comparable or endpoint-mismatched (e.g., PGS000767 putamen volume; PGS000907 antidepressant side-effect context), making cross-candidate performance ranking uncertain from the provided metadata alone.

All 8 candidates are direct matches to dilated cardiomyopathy by trait_efo, with endpoint fidelity best judged by phenotyping_reported. The strongest endpoint-aligned options are the 2024 Nat Genet disease-focused family with explicit clinical DCM phenotyping (PGS004950/PGS004951). Between these siblings, PGS004951 (MTAG) is mildly preferred per provided domain guidance that MTAG-enhanced variants are generally stronger within the same study family, and it also shows higher reported discrimination/effect size than its non-MTAG counterpart (univariate PRS-only AUC 0.67 vs 0.64; OR 1.93 vs 1.71) with similarly basic covariates (sex, PCs). Main limitation: performance reporting is not fully comparable across all candidates (some report full-model AUROC/R² with different covariate sets and some have evaluation ancestry strings that are ambiguous), so while PGS004951 is best-supported within the most endpoint-faithful subgroup, certainty is not maximal.

All 5 candidates are direct matches to diverticular disease via trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (including ICD10 K57 and diverticular disease/diverticulitis). Among models with PRS-comparable metrics, PGS000997 (snpnet; TTE diverticular disease of intestine) reports the strongest PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC no covariates 0.591; PGS R2 no covariates 0.01777) and the largest incremental AUROC (0.01733) in European validation, with PRS-only R2 consistent with the provided heritability ceiling sanity-check (local h2_liability ~0.0174). Competing models either come from the same pan-trait UKB framework but with weaker PRS-only metrics (PGS000996), or lack PRS-comparable metrics entirely and only provide OR/full-model AUROC with potentially non-comparable covariates (PGS004474/PGS004544 have unknown covariates and only OR~1.31; PGS004614 reports only full-model AUROC 0.76 with covariates including family history). Remaining limitation: PGS000997’s endpoint is time-to-event (a mild endpoint-fidelity warning for generic disease risk) and it is from a pan-trait framework paper, so despite being best-supported on available PRS-only metrics, the overall evidence package is not unequivocally high-quality versus newer disease-focused alternatives whose PRS-only metrics are missing.

All three candidates are direct matches for the target trait (all map to EFO: Dupuytren Contracture; phenotyping_reported is Dupuytren’s contracture / contracture of palmar fascia [Dupuytren’s disease]). However, the evidence is limited/conflicted because the two portability-framework models (PGS001880, PGS002092) report only partial correlation (no PRS-only AUROC/R²), while the sparse pan-trait UKB framework model (PGS001254; “across 813 traits”) reports AUROC/R² but is structurally a very sparse framework score (11 variants, snpnet) that domain guidance flags as often generalizing poorly. Between the two portability siblings from the same publication with essentially identical endpoint/covariates/ancestry evaluation, PGS002092 (LDpred2; 484,484 variants) has slightly higher partial-r (0.0797 vs 0.0783) and a method/variant-count profile more consistent with capturing polygenic signal than the penalized-regression 2,443-variant alternative, making it the best-supported direct-match choice from the visible metadata. Confidence is not high because key comparable discrimination metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²) are missing for the selected model and the remaining candidates come from framework-style studies rather than clearly disease-focused multi-cohort development.

All four candidates map to the target via trait_efo=follicular lymphoma, but endpoint fidelity differs. PGS002304 has direct phenotype alignment (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both “Follicular lymphoma”) and provides the strongest available discrimination evidence in this context (AUROC 0.61 with CI 0.59–0.63 in European validation). By contrast, PGS000643/PGS000644 have phenotyping_reported “Nodular lymphoma” (near-synonymous but not exact) and show much weaker AUROC (~0.53–0.54) despite clean/basic covariates; PGS003455 has an explicit phenotype mismatch (phenotyping_reported “Chronic lymphocytic leukemia”) and lacks usable discrimination metrics. The main limitation is that PGS002304 reports only a full-model AUROC with covariates listed as “Unknown” and has a small validation sample size (n=197), so PRS-only performance and covariate comparability cannot be confirmed from the provided metadata, lowering confidence.

All 15 candidates are direct matches to glaucoma or its dominant subtype primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG), with phenotype alignment generally acceptable (many explicitly use POAG or glaucoma endpoints). Among candidates with comparable endpoint fidelity, PGS001792 is best supported by a combination of (i) disease-specific endpoint (phenotyping_reported: POAG), (ii) a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto) with very large variant count (911,402), and (iii) reported validation discrimination (full-model AUROC=0.777) plus a PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.03209), which is below the provided glaucoma liability h2 ceiling (0.0556) and therefore passes the heritability sanity check. However, the overall decision remains sub-optimal because performance reporting is heterogeneous across models (many lack PRS-only AUROC/R2), some reported AUROCs are full-model and not directly comparable across differing covariate sets, and the strongest-looking AUROC in the pool (PGS000137 full-model AUROC=0.8) is paired with family history covariate (a comparability concern) and lacks PRS-only metrics—leaving residual uncertainty about which model has the best standalone PRS performance.

Multiple direct-match gout PRS candidates are present. PGS001248 is preferred because it has a direct gout endpoint (trait_efo=gout; phenotyping_reported=Gout) and, unlike most other gout candidates shown, reports PRS-comparable performance (PGS-only AUROC=0.66908 and PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.04014) plus incremental AUROC (0.04061), enabling more interpretable PRS contribution than models reporting only full-model AUROC or only effect sizes. A key limitation is that PGS001248 comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework study ('across 813 traits'), which domain guidance flags as often less reliable for external generalization; additionally, several other gout models show higher full-model AUROC (e.g., PGS000199 AUROC=0.85 with unknown covariates; PGS004265–PGS004269 ~0.797–0.799 with basic covariates), but these are not directly comparable PRS-only metrics and may be covariate-influenced. This leaves residual uncertainty, so the direct-match choice is supported but not clearly definitive.

All three candidates are direct matches for Hashimoto’s thyroiditis (trait_efo = Hashimoto’s thyroiditis; phenotyping_reported = lymphocytic thyroiditis) and come from the same publication family with the same evaluation ancestry set and validation sample size, so endpoint alignment and transportability context do not clearly differentiate them. None reports PRS-only (covariate-free) discrimination; the available AUROC values appear to be full-model AUROC with covariates listed as Unknown, which limits comparability and makes small AUROC differences weak evidence. Given that limitation, PGS005271 is preferred because it shows the strongest effect-size evidence (OR per SD ≈ 1.55, meeting the domain-knowledge ‘strong’ threshold) while also using a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRSCS) with a large variant count (~1.085M), which is structurally favorable for polygenic traits. Confidence is moderate (not high) because covariates are unknown and the reported AUROC is full-model rather than PRS-only, and because sibling models from the same study family have similar validation context with only modest metric differences.

Multiple direct-match candidates exist for the target trait (heart failure), including several with trait_efo=heart failure and phenotyping_reported as prevalent/incident heart failure. Among these, PGS005097 has strong endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: prevalent heart failure; trait_efo: heart failure) and comes from a disease-focused, multi-cohort heart-failure genetics study with broad training_development_cohorts (including HERMES, MVP, FinnGen, eMERGE, etc.). It also reports a representative validation AUROC (0.72 with CI) plus an additional metric (Brier skill score 0.065), providing more directly comparable performance evidence than many other heart-failure-labeled models that report only effect sizes or lack discrimination metrics. However, the pool contains several CHF PheCode models (PGS005074/076/077/078/080/083/084/085) with higher reported full-model C-index (~0.75) and stronger ORs (~1.44–1.46), and one heart-failure model with PRS-comparable R2 reported (PGS001790; Nagelkerke R2 covariates-regressed-out 0.006981). Because many reported AUC/C-index values are full-model metrics with differing covariate sets (often not PRS-only), and covariates are unknown for some candidates, the evidence is insufficient to declare a single clearly best model without unresolved comparability concerns; thus the selection is direct-match but sub-optimal rather than high-confidence.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to hip osteoarthritis by trait_efo, but they differ materially in endpoint fidelity and PRS-comparable performance evidence. PGS002763 has the cleanest phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported: "Hip osteoarthritis" rather than proxy endpoints like total hip replacement) and provides a PRS-relevant effect size (OR=1.38 per SD, 95% CI 1.31–1.46), which is moderate discriminative evidence in the absence of PRS-only AUROC/R². Competing options have notable limitations: PGS000967 is from a pan-trait UKB sparse framework ("across 813 traits") and its strong-looking full-model AUROC (0.69) is likely covariate-influenced given small incremental AUROC (0.00918) and low PGS-only R² (0.00628), making it weaker as standalone PRS evidence; PGS002728 and PGS002750 use hip replacement/total hip replacement endpoints (treatment/proxy), and PGS004478/PGS004548 have unknown covariates with only modest ORs. Confidence is not high because no candidate reports clearly PRS-only discrimination metrics (AUC/R²) on a comparable endpoint, so selection relies mainly on endpoint fidelity plus moderate OR evidence.

Direct-match Hodgkin lymphoma candidates are present (PGS000637/PGS000638/PGS000639/PGS000640 and PGS003449). Among the PRSweb Hodgkin’s disease siblings with consistent phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported: “Hodgkin’s disease”; trait_efo: Hodgkins lymphoma; EUR GWAS/DEV/EVAL; basic covariates age/sex/batch/PCs), PGS000639 (P+T, 20 variants) shows the strongest reported validation metrics in this context (full_model_auc=0.62; Nagelkerke R²=0.0276; OR per SD=1.476 [1.154–1.889]), outperforming the other PRSweb Hodgkin models (AUC 0.569–0.601; OR 1.292–1.377). PGS003449 is label-aligned (“Hodgkin lymphoma”) but has an apparent endpoint inconsistency (phenotyping_reported listed as “Chronic lymphocytic leukemia”) and provides only a weak effect size (OR=1.02) with no AUC/R², so it is not better supported than the coherent PRSweb cluster. Overall outcome is sub-optimal because the available discrimination evidence is largely full-model (not explicitly PGS-only), and the best-supported candidate’s performance is modest with wide uncertainty in some reported metrics (e.g., top 1% OR CI).

Multiple direct-match hypertension models are present (e.g., PGS000706, PGS001320, PGS001838, PGS002047, PGS004234, PGS004236, PGS004934). Among these, PGS004236 is a direct hypertension endpoint (trait_efo=hypertension; phenotyping_reported=prevalent hypertension) and is structurally favored by the domain guidance because it is an explicit multi-score aggregation approach (PRSsum) with broad multi-ethnic evaluation (European, African American/Afro-Caribbean, Hispanic/Latin American, Asian unspecified) and reports strong effect size evidence (OR=2.1, 95% CI 1.99–2.21). Competing direct-match options include UKB pan-trait/framework-style snpnet models (PGS001320; PGS000706) with lower reported AUROC (~0.62–0.72 full-model) and the UKB portability framework models (PGS001838/PGS002047) that report only partial correlation without discrimination metrics; these provide weaker or less directly comparable PRS-quality evidence. Main limitation: PGS004236’s reported AUROC is full-model (0.764) with multiple covariates (including BMI and smoking), and no explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2 is provided, so the magnitude of standalone PRS discrimination cannot be cleanly compared across candidates; this keeps confidence at Moderate despite strong endpoint alignment and effect-size support.

All 7 candidates are direct matches for a hyperthyroidism target via near-synonymous endpoints (hyperthyroidism/thyrotoxicosis) or the clinically dominant subtype Graves’ disease (explicitly supported as a strong direct match in the provided domain_knowledge). However, the pool is split between (a) UKB pan-trait/framework-derived sparse snpnet scores with explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS001042/PGS001043) and (b) Graves’ disease multi-biobank scores with only full-model AUROC and unknown covariates (PGS005264–PGS005266), plus UKB portability scores with only partial-r (PGS001815/PGS002023). Given the domain_knowledge warning that the “813 traits” sparse UKB framework scores often generalize poorly, and the Graves’ disease scores lacking PRS-only metrics and having unknown covariates (making their AUROC less comparable), the evidence does not cleanly identify a single high-quality winner. Among the two most endpoint-faithful hyperthyroidism-labeled models with the most directly PRS-comparable reporting, PGS001043 is preferred over PGS001042 because it matches the target label explicitly (hyperthyroidism/thyrotoxicosis) and has essentially identical PRS-only AUROC/R² and incremental AUROC under basic covariates, with no major conflicts visible. Remaining limitation: no candidate provides clearly superior, PRS-only performance evidence from a disease-focused multi-cohort study with clean covariate reporting, so the best choice remains uncertain.

All four candidates are direct matches on concept (trait_efo = hypertrophic cardiomyopathy). Endpoint fidelity favors PGS004910/PGS004911 and PGS000739 because their phenotyping_reported is the disease itself, whereas PGS000778 targets clinical events among pathogenic sarcomeric-variant carriers (a restricted subgroup/prognosis-like endpoint), making it less directly aligned for general HCM risk. Between the two 2025 Nat Genet PRS-CS siblings (PGS004910 vs PGS004911), covariates are similarly basic (age, age^2, sex, PC1-10) and endpoints match; PGS004911 reports stronger validation performance (full-model AUROC 0.80 vs 0.73; R² 0.048 vs 0.031; higher HR/OR), and domain guidance mildly prefers the MTAG-enhanced variant when otherwise comparable. Main limitation: the reported AUROC/R² appear to be full-model metrics (not explicitly PRS-only), so cross-model comparability is imperfect and confidence is reduced accordingly.

All listed candidates are direct matches at the trait/EFO level (hypothyroidism), but several have endpoint-fidelity limitations (e.g., therapy-induced hypothyroidism in cancer patients: PGS000759/PGS000761/PGS000820). Among the generic disease-endpoint models, PGS000965 (Hypothyroidism/myxoedema) provides the strongest PRS-comparable performance evidence in the context: it reports both PGS-only AUROC (0.689) and PGS-only R² (0.0727) plus full-model AUROC (0.768) in a European validation, whereas many other direct-match candidates report only effect sizes or only full-model AUROC without PRS-only metrics. A key limitation is that PGS000965 comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework study ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as often less externally robust than disease-focused scores; additionally, the very high-AUC disease-focused PGS005218 cannot be fairly compared because its AUROC is likely covariate-inflated (includes TSH/T4/anti-TPO) and lacks PGS-only metrics in the provided record. Given these tradeoffs, PGS000965 is best-supported by the visible, PRS-comparable metrics, but confidence is moderated by the framework-origin penalty and incomplete comparability across the remaining candidates.

Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS001823, PGS002031), both aligned to the target via trait_efo="iron metabolism disease" and phenotyping_reported/trait_reported="Disorders of iron metabolism", with similar basic covariates and identical training/validation context (UKB-derived portability study; DEV EUR; EVAL includes multiple ancestries; selected validation ancestry European; validation_sample_size n=19,883). Performance evidence is limited to partial correlation (partial-r) from the selected European validation record; PGS002031 is slightly higher (0.1355 [0.1219, 0.1492]) than PGS001823 (0.1307 [0.117, 0.1444]), though CIs overlap so the advantage is modest. With endpoint fidelity and covariates essentially identical, this small but consistent metric edge supports selecting PGS002031 as best among the direct matches; confidence is moderate because the performance difference is small and no PRS-only AUROC/R2 or effect sizes are provided to strengthen separation.

All four candidates are direct-match models within the juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) disease family, but only PGS000114 targets the umbrella endpoint aligned to the target trait: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported are all Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis. The other three models (PGS000324/325/326) are explicitly JIA subtypes (enthesitis-related, oligoarticular, RF-negative polyarthritis), which are less endpoint-faithful for a generic JIA target despite some having higher full-model AUROC. PGS000114 also reports supportive validation evidence in Europeans (full-model AUROC 0.738 with basic covariates: sex and PCs; OR per SD 2.085), and comes from the same disease-focused publication family as the subtype scores, making it the most coherent direct-match choice. Main limitation: the reported AUROC appears to be a full-model metric (not explicitly PGS-only), so standalone PRS discrimination cannot be cleanly compared across candidates; however, endpoint fidelity dominates here.

All 10 candidates are direct matches for the target concept (kidney/renal cancer), including clinically dominant subtype mappings (renal cell carcinoma). Among them, PGS004908 has the strongest visible PRS-discrimination evidence: it reports an OR per SD of 1.5 (95% CI 1.43–1.58), which is materially stronger than the ~1.15 OR/HR per SD reported for several other candidates (e.g., PGS000076/PGS000787/PGS000605/PGS000606), and it also shows the highest reported AUROC (0.74, EUR evaluation). Phenotyping_reported is directly ‘Kidney cancer’ and covariates are standard epidemiologic/demographic adjustments (age, sex, PCs, BMI, smoking, hypertension), which are not flagged as heavy leakage in the provided domain guidance. Main limitation: the AUROC shown is a full-model metric (no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2), so cross-model comparability is imperfect and confidence is reduced despite the strong per-SD OR and coherent endpoint alignment.

Direct-match candidates for kidney failure are present (notably PGS000708 with trait_reported/trait_efo = kidney failure, and PGS004492/PGS004562 with trait_efo = kidney failure and phenotyping_reported = N18 chronic renal failure). PGS000708 is preferred because its phenotyping_reported is a direct kidney-failure endpoint (diabetic kidney failure) and it provides the most informative validation performance evidence among the kidney-failure-labeled options (European validation with C-index 0.779 and HR 1.19). However, the recommendation is sub-optimal because the endpoint is restricted to diabetic kidney failure (not generic kidney failure), and the reported discrimination is a full-model metric with covariates (age/sex/PCs etc.) rather than an explicit PRS-only AUROC/R²; competing kidney-failure candidates (PGS004492/PGS004562) have unknown covariates and lack comparable discrimination metrics, preventing a high-confidence selection.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to knee osteoarthritis/gonarthrosis, but most lack PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²) and/or have unclear covariates, making it hard to identify a clearly best-supported model. PGS001192 has strong endpoint alignment (EFO: osteoarthritis, knee; phenotyping: TTE gonarthrosis) and is the only candidate reporting explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates=0.5566; PGS R² no covariates=0.0068) plus incremental AUROC (0.0104), enabling a heritability sanity check (PGS R² well below h2_obs=0.0219) and more comparable assessment than models reporting only full-model AUROC or only OR/HR. Main limitation: it is a time-to-event endpoint from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (snpnet across 813 traits), which domain guidance flags as often less externally robust than disease-focused multi-cohort scores; however, the disease-focused alternatives here (e.g., PGS002729, PGS002767, PGS004479/PGS004549, PGS004883) do not provide PRS-only metrics in the visible evidence, so their apparent full-model AUROC/OR/HR cannot be cleanly compared to PRS001192’s PRS-only performance.

All 5 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo, but their endpoint fidelity and PRS-comparable performance evidence differ. PGS000053 (and its sibling PGS000054) has the cleanest disease-endpoint alignment via phenotyping_reported = "Familial late-onset Alzheimer's disease (LOAD)" and uses only basic covariates (age, sex). It also reports an interpretable per-SD effect size (OR=1.29, 95% CI 1.21–1.37) in European evaluation, providing some PRS-discrimination evidence when AUC/R2 are missing. Competing models have notable limitations: PGS002289’s phenotyping_reported is a cognition test interaction endpoint rather than AD diagnosis; PGS000334 reports R²=0.191 from a C+T pipeline with unknown covariates, which is difficult to interpret and potentially non-comparable given the provided heritability ceiling context; PGS004918 reports only a full-model AUROC (0.731) with unknown covariates and very small validation (n=136), so it is not reliable as PRS-only evidence. Remaining limitation: PGS000053 lacks PRS-only AUROC/R² and is framed as familial LOAD, so while it is the best-supported direct-match here, the overall evidence package is not strong enough for a high-confidence pick.

Direct-match candidates for lung cancer are present (multiple models with trait_reported/phenotyping_reported as lung cancer or closely overlapping endpoints such as lung and bronchus cancer). Among these, PGS000078 has strong endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: incident lung cancer; trait_efo: lung carcinoma), large-scale disease-focused multi-cohort development/validation context (many lung-cancer cohorts listed; validation_sample_size n=392,539; EUR GWAS/EVAL), and includes an effect size (HR 1.16, 95% CI 1.11–1.22) alongside reported discrimination (AUROC 0.846, C-index 0.849). However, the reported AUROC/C-index are full-model metrics with extensive covariates (including detailed smoking variables, PM2.5, and family history), and no explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2 is provided; per domain guidance this limits comparability and prevents a high-confidence claim that the PRS itself is best. Competing direct-match models either have weaker/less informative performance evidence (many PRSweb models with AUROC ~0.52–0.54), are endpoint-restricted (e.g., early-onset <50 years PGS000740; never-smoker women EAS PGS004164/PGS004165), or have unclear/suspect reporting (e.g., PGS000789 lists full_model_r2=0.799, which is not interpretable as PRS-only and conflicts with heritability sanity-check expectations). Therefore PGS000078 is the best-supported direct match from the visible evidence, but overall evidence remains limited by lack of PRS-only metrics and covariate-heavy evaluation.

Direct-match candidates are present for lupus erythematosus (including models mapped to systemic lupus erythematosus and two models explicitly mapped to lupus erythematosus). Among the lupus-erythematosus–mapped options, PGS002082 has the strongest structural properties (LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage with 361,553 variants) and reports a slightly higher PRS-comparable metric (partial-r 0.0212, European validation record) than the sibling portability score PGS001870 (partial-r 0.0184; 87 variants). However, the evidence remains limited for a clearly high-quality pick because (i) both PGS001870/PGS002082 come from a portability framework paper rather than a disease-focused SLE study, and (ii) across the broader direct-match set, several SLE models report higher AUROC but these are full-model AUROCs with unknown or potentially non-comparable covariates (and one uses phenotype risk score covariate), making cross-model performance comparisons unreliable from the provided metadata alone.

There are multiple direct-match candidates for lymphoid leukemia (e.g., PGS000077, PGS000645, PGS000788, PGS002305) plus several chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) subtype scores. For the broad target “lymphoid leukemia,” the best endpoint-aligned options are those with phenotyping_reported as incident lymphocytic/lymphoid leukemia (PGS000077, PGS000788) or lymphoid leukemia (PGS000645). Among these, PGS000788 shows the strongest visible effect-size evidence (HR=1.7 per SD, 95% CI 1.53–1.88) and slightly higher reported full-model discrimination (AUROC 0.738; C-index 0.756) with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), and it is evaluated in a large European cohort (n=391,338). However, confidence is limited because the reported AUROC/C-index are full-model metrics (no PGS-only AUROC/R2), and PGS000788 is described as an inverse-weight reparameterization of PGS000077 rather than an independently derived score, making the apparent performance edge potentially non-comparable; additionally, several CLL-specific models (e.g., PGS000648/PGS000646/PGS000874) have strong metrics but are subtype/restricted-endpoint matches rather than clearly best for the umbrella trait.

All 7 candidates are direct matches at the concept level (macular degeneration / age-related macular degeneration). Prioritizing endpoint fidelity, PGS004606 has the cleanest disease-endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: "Age-related macular degeneration") and provides supportive discrimination evidence (full-model AUROC=0.71) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs 1–10). It also reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.76), which is explicitly noted in the provided domain knowledge as a meaningful indicator of PRS discriminative power when PRS-only AUC/R² are unavailable. Competing models are weaker on at least one key dimension: PGS001013 is from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework and shows low PRS-only performance (PGS-only AUROC ~0.553; PGS-only R² ~0.006); PGS001834/PGS002041 are portability-framework scores with only small partial correlations (~0.016–0.018); PGS002269 has phenotype mismatch (retinal layer thickness proxy rather than AMD diagnosis); PGS004607 is an AFR-GWAS-derived score with lower reported AUROC (0.65) in EUR evaluation; PGS004952 reports an implausibly formatted AUROC in classification_metrics (84.2) and has a small validation sample (n=1,232), making its performance evidence ambiguous despite endpoint relevance (late AMD). Main limitation: across the pool, PRS-only comparable metrics are largely missing for the disease-focused candidates (including PGS004606), so confidence is moderated because selection relies on effect size plus full-model AUROC rather than explicit PRS-only AUROC/R².

Direct-match melanoma PRS candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo=melanoma / phenotyping_reported melanoma or incident melanoma). Among these, PGS002247 is a direct endpoint match (phenotyping_reported: incident invasive melanoma; trait_efo: melanoma; EUR GWAS/EVAL) with comparatively strong reported discrimination in the provided context (full_model AUROC 0.691 with R² 0.072). However, selection remains sub-optimal because most candidates report only full-model metrics (not explicitly PGS-only AUROC/R²), making cross-model performance comparability limited; additionally, there is meaningful competition from other direct-match models with similar endpoints and metrics (e.g., PGS002246 AUROC 0.688; PGS002253 AUROC 0.662; PGS000743 AUROC 0.74 but with heavy traditional risk-factor covariates and much smaller validation n), so the evidence does not uniquely identify a single clearly superior PRS without unresolved comparability concerns.

All six candidates are nominal direct matches on concept fields (trait_reported/trait_efo indicate multiple myeloma / plasma cell myeloma), but endpoint fidelity differs: PGS003450 has an explicit phenotyping mismatch (phenotyping_reported = Chronic lymphocytic leukemia), making it a weak direct-match despite the trait label. Among the remaining models, PGS002281 and PGS002306 report higher full-model AUROC than the PRSweb scores (PGS000652/653/654), with PGS002306 highest (AUROC 0.69) but based on a much smaller validation sample (n=290) and unknown covariates, reducing interpretability/comparability. PGS002281 shows strong and more stable-looking evidence with European validation n=2,395, full-model AUROC 0.644 (CI 0.622–0.666), and a substantial risk gradient (OR 3.18 highest vs lowest quintiles), with covariates disclosed as basic demographics/region. However, none of the candidates provide explicit PRS-only (covariate-free) AUROC/R², so the apparent AUROC advantages may be partly covariate-driven and cross-model comparability remains limited; therefore the best available direct match is selected with only moderate confidence.

All 7 listed candidates are direct matches to multiple sclerosis by trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (mostly “Multiple sclerosis”; one is time-to-event). The strongest PRS-comparable performance evidence is for PGS001270, which reports explicit PGS-only AUROC (0.65856) and PGS R2 (no covariates) (0.02904), plus incremental AUROC (0.08355) under basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), making it more interpretable for PRS quality than candidates that report only full-model AUROC (e.g., PGS002726 AUROC 0.8 with covariates unknown; PGS000809 AUROC 0.765 with only full-model metrics) or only partial-r (PGS001831/PGS002038). Limitation: PGS001270 comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as tending to generalize poorly versus disease-focused scores; meanwhile some disease-focused MS studies show higher full-model AUROC/OR but lack PRS-only metrics and/or have unclear covariates, preventing a high-confidence best-in-class selection from the visible evidence.

Direct-match myocardial infarction candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo=myocardial infarction / acute myocardial infarction). Among the MI-specific options, PGS005039 (Myocardial infarction, PheCode 411.2) has the strongest visible validation discrimination in the provided set (C-index 0.7848 in European validation) and a strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.578, 95% CI 1.50–1.67), supporting meaningful PRS signal; its covariates (age, sex, 20 PCs) are basic and comparable. Competing MI-specific models from the UKB pan-trait sparse framework (PGS001314/001315/001316/001317) report PRS-only metrics but are from a framework study family flagged as less reliable for external generalization, and their PRS-only AUROC (~0.58–0.60) is not clearly superior. Other MI-labeled candidates (e.g., PGS004458/PGS004528 acute MI) lack comparable discrimination metrics and have unknown covariates, lowering interpretability. Overall, selection is sub-optimal rather than high-quality because many candidates report only full-model C-index (not explicitly PRS-only), and the MVP-derived PGS0050xx family contains several near-tied siblings with very similar C-index values, making it hard to assert a uniquely best model from the visible metadata alone.

Both candidates are direct matches to the target trait with identical endpoint fidelity: `phenotyping_reported` is ICD10 J33 (Nasal polyp) and `trait_efo` is Nasal Cavity Polyp for both, with the same EUR-only development/evaluation context and same publication family. Neither reports PRS-comparable AUC/R2, so selection must rely on the available effect-size evidence and structural/method signals. PGS004535 reports a stronger per-SD odds ratio (OR=1.600668) than PGS004465 (OR=1.3496), and domain guidance treats OR≥1.5 as strong discriminative evidence, making PGS004535 the better-supported choice. All three candidates are direct-match on trait_efo=preeclampsia, but endpoint fidelity differs. All three candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo (vitiligo), but they differ materially in endpoint fidelity and PRS-comparable performance evidence. PGS001536 has the most directly interpretable PRS performance reporting for generic vitiligo risk: it provides explicit PGS-only metrics (PGS AUROC 0.64193; PGS R2 0.01621) plus incremental AUROC (0.08163) with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), and its PGS-only R2 is plausibly below the provided EUR heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.1738), supporting metric sanity. In contrast, PGS000760’s phenotyping_reported is therapy-specific (anti-PD-L1 induced hypothyroidism in cancer patients), making it a weaker vitiligo endpoint despite an HR=1.41; and PGS000738 shows an apparent endpoint mismatch (phenotyping_reported: Red hair) and lacks PRS-only AUC/R2, reducing confidence in its relevance and comparability. Remaining limitation: PGS001536 is from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (snpnet across 813 traits) and uses a time-to-event vitiligo endpoint, both of which the provided domain guidance flags as potential generalization/endpoint-fidelity weaknesses versus a clearly disease-focused vitiligo study—so while it is best-supported among the visible options, the overall direct-match evidence is not unequivocally high-quality.
